summary: Tonga's Ministry of Revenue and Customs lists the countries whose citizens may be issued a 30 day visitor visa on arrival — among them Australia, Canada, Ireland, Japan, New Zealand, the United Kingdom and the United States — subject to conditions including a valid return ticket and sufficient funds, and says citizens of all other countries need visas to enter Tonga (prior to arrival). The EU–Tonga visa waiver agreement provides visa-free travel for citizens of the Union for a maximum of 90 days in any 180-day period, and does not apply to Ireland. China's Foreign Ministry lists a mutual visa exemption with Tonga for ordinary passports, under which holders may stay for less than 30 days.

notes: The UK government says you must declare any personal valuables worth 500 Tongan pa'anga or more.
The UK government says the maximum penalty for importing or exporting illegal drugs is 30 years' hard labour and fines of several hundred thousand US dollars.

safety.text: The UK government says the level of serious crime is low, but petty theft is fairly common. It says the tropical cyclone season normally runs from November to May, and that Tonga is part of the Pacific Ring of Fire, where earthquakes and volcanic activity can happen at any time.

bestTimeToVisit.text: The UK government says the tropical cyclone season normally runs from November to May, but cyclones can happen throughout the year (Canada's travel advice says cyclones are more likely between November and April), and that whales frequent the waters of Tonga every year between June and November. No official source we could read names a best season.

idp.text: Tonga's Traffic Act 2020 (section 17), published by the Attorney General's Office, says a person who holds a valid driving licence issued by a country that recognises a valid Tongan driving licence in return may drive the same class of motor vehicle in Tonga, on the conditions that licence carries, for a period of not more than 12 months. tips.text: The UK government says people in Tonga strictly observe the Sabbath, and that on Sundays local people may consider recreational activities to be disrespectful, except at island resorts.

The UK government says topless sunbathing and nudity in public are illegal, with fines of up to 100 pa'anga or a prison sentence of up to 4 months for refusing to pay, and that swimwear is acceptable on the beach or by streams and waterfalls but in other areas is likely to receive negative attention.

The UK government says it is illegal to swim or kayak with whales unless you are on a licensed boat with a certified guide, with a fine of up to 5,000 pa'anga or an 18-month prison sentence, or both, and that whales frequent the waters of Tonga every year between June and November.

The UK government says the tropical cyclone season normally runs from November to May but cyclones can happen throughout the year, and that Tonga is part of the Pacific Ring of Fire, where earthquakes and volcanic activity can happen at any time and trigger tsunamis.
Canada's travel advice says ATMs are available on Tongatapu, especially in Nuku'alofa, and that foreign currency exchange services may be limited on other islands.

faq.question: Do I need a visa for Tonga?
faq.answer: Not in advance if your country is on Tonga's list: Tonga's Ministry of Revenue and Customs says citizens of the listed countries — among them the US, UK, Canada, Australia, New Zealand, Japan, Singapore and Ireland — may be issued a 30 day visitor visa on arrival, and that citizens of all other countries need visas to enter Tonga (prior to arrival). The EU–Tonga visa waiver agreement provides visa-free travel for citizens of the Union for a maximum of 90 days in any 180-day period, and does not apply to Ireland. China's Foreign Ministry lists a mutual visa exemption with Tonga for ordinary passports, under which holders may stay for less than 30 days.

faq.question: How long can I stay on the visa on arrival?
faq.answer: Tonga's Ministry of Revenue and Customs says citizens of the listed countries may be issued a 30 day visitor visa on arrival, on condition of a valid return ticket out of Tonga and sufficient funds, and that passports must be valid for a minimum of 6 months when entering Tonga. The UK government tells British citizens they may also need to show confirmed accommodation. To extend your stay, the Ministry says to contact the Immigration Department.

faq.question: Can I extend my stay in Tonga?
faq.answer: Tonga's Ministry of Revenue and Customs says to contact the Immigration Department in Neiafu, Vava'u, or in Nuku'alofa (Salote Road) to extend your stay, and that all non-Tongan passport holders shall ensure their visas remain valid for any period for which they are in the Kingdom. No official source we could read states how long an extension lasts or the maximum total stay.

faq.question: Is everything really closed on Sunday in Tonga?
faq.answer: The UK government says people in Tonga strictly observe the Sabbath and that on Sundays local people may consider recreational activities to be disrespectful, which does not apply to island resorts; Canada's travel advice says any recreational activity on Sundays outside island resorts may be seen as provocative.

faq.question: Can I pay by card in Tonga?
faq.answer: Canada's travel advice says most major hotels and some restaurants and stores accept credit cards, ATMs are available on Tongatapu, especially in Nuku'alofa, and foreign currency exchange may be limited on other islands.
